lens.message:
Here's the shift: we went from holding nothing about the Kestrelwood's frequency to holding a settled, verified baseline — 88.4 MHz, checked against the June reference plates, holding across the full observing band. It changes how we approach judging Kestrelwood observations (every reading now gets read against 88.4 MHz, band-wide), checking future drift (measured against the June plates, not ad hoc), and what counts as settled about the instrument.

One section, before and after —

As written (Quill, 2026-07-06): "The Kestrelwood spectrograph is now calibrated at 88.4 MHz. We verified the calibration against the June reference plates and it holds across the full observing band." — a status note from the session.

As it reads now: this is where the baseline gets minted. 88.4 MHz stops being a number in a log and becomes the standing reference every Kestrelwood observation is judged against; the June reference plates fix the yardstick any future drift check measures by; a reading that doesn't fit the band now points at calibration first, not at the sky.

Right lens?

Where it lands: here only, honestly. The stream has no other documents — nothing in the index to move — so this shift currently lives in this conversation alone. When observing logs or calibration records join the stream, this is the line they get checked against.

Affected documents: none.

Nothing to apply across yet. Once documents land on this stream, I can carry this baseline through them — say the word.
